newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-NAMIBIA'S FAIRYTALE COMES TRUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAMIBIA'S FAIRYTALE COMES TRUE.

text.p: Namibia achieved a fairytale qualification for the African Nations Cup on Sunday as the line-up for the 16-team finals tournament was completed with the weekend's last round of qualifying matches.

The tiny southern African nation, with fewer than 8,000 registered footballers, forced a 1-1 draw in Gabon to secure a first-ever place in the Nations Cup finals just five years after joining world football.
The point was enough to give them second place in group five and qualification for the tournament in Burkina Faso next February.
Algeria, Angola, Egypt, Ivory Coast and the new Democratic Republic of Congo also secured qualification on Sunday while Mozambique won through with a dramatic 2-1 home win over Malawi on Saturday.

Namibia grabbed the spotlight with their draw in Libreville, where Johannes Hindjou scored the all-important goal in the second half after captain Pierre Aubame's penalty had put Gabon ahead at halftime.

Namibia had an opportunity two weeks ago to secure qualification but lost at home to Cameroon, leaving them with the arduous task of avoiding defeat in Libreville against their rival for the runners-up spot.
But a gutsy performance, characterised by swift counter attacks, allowed Namibia to record a famous victory with Hindjou showing great composure from the penalty spot for the equaliser.
Namibia will be the only debutants at the finals, for which hosts Burkina Faso, holders South Africa, Cameroon, Ghana, Guinea, Morocco, Togo, Tunisia and Zambia had already qualified.
Former winners Algeria and Egypt both scraped through on Sunday, winning their home matches and seeing their nearest rivals lose away.
Egypt thrashed Ethiopia 8-1 in Cairo, the first two goals coming in the opening five minutes, and then saw Morocco do them a big favour by beating Senegal 3-0 in Rabat.
Moroccan's Salaheddine Bassir scored twice to end the qualifying competition as the leading marksman with five goals.
Algeria won as expected against Benin with two first-half goals in Algiers on Sunday but only secured qualification when Mali failed to win in the Ivory Coast.

A 4-2 win in Bouake for the Ivorians, with two goals from veteran striker Joel Tiehi, ensured top place in group two for the 1992 champions with Algeria runners-up, a point ahead of the crestfallen Malians.

Angola got the three points they needed to ensure a place in Burkina Faso when they beat Zimbabwe 2-1 in Luanda to leapfrog their fellow southern Africans. The goals came from former Benfica strikers players Paulao and Akwa.
Stewart Murisa pulled a goal back with 12 minutes left to give Zimbabwe a glimmer of hope but time ran out on their hopes of a first-ever place in the finals.

The Democratic Republic of Congo also won through with their first win since the country changed its name from Zaire. Nzangani Kidoda's 15th minute goal gave the home team a 1-0 win over Togo in Kinshasa for a one-point advantage over Liberia in group six. George Weah's team lost out despite beating Tanzania in Monrovia.
Mozambique pulled off a miraculous comeback victory on Saturday in Maputo in their group seven tie against Malawi.
Malawi needed just a point to qualify and went ahead through recalled striker Jones Nkhwazi midway through the second half.
But with five minutes left Pinto Barros equalised and Tico-Tico hit the winner two minutes later.
Cameroon and Kenya drew 1-1 in a game of little importance in group five in Yaounde with Fabrice Moreau converting an injury time penalty for the hosts.

Kenya lead from early in the second half through Francis Were and were on course to become the first country ever to beat Cameroon at home in a Nations Cup before the Spanish-based midfielder equalised.
